extracted.intended_audience: researchers and meta-researchers conducting systematic or literature reviews on spin/publication bias in biomedical literature; journal editors, clinicians and policymakers interested in research integrity
extracted.subtask_short: meta-research on spin in biomedical literature
extracted.subtask_description: Protocol for a meta-research study that identifies reported patterns of 'spin', assesses their prevalence across previously published systematic or literature reviews in biomedicine, and rates the seriousness of their impact using a Delphi consensus. Includes search, eligibility, data extraction, quality assessment, statistical pooling rules and a Delphi procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of spin
rubrics_metrics.description: Spin is defined as reporting practices that distort the interpretation of results and create misleading conclusions by suggesting more favourable results. It can be intentional or unintentional, inaccurate, unfair or partial reporting practices that distort interpretation and create misleading conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spin may flatter research and make it more attractive for publication and citation, leading to overpromising and misleading information; it negatively affects research reproducibility, clinical practice, policy, and resource allocation. Examples: claiming beneficial effect in a title not supported by findings; conclusions not supported by reported findings; recommendations for practice inconsistent with study conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three main forms/classification of spin
rubrics_metrics.description: Spin patterns can be classified into three main forms: misleading reporting, misleading interpretation and inappropriate extrapolation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Misleading reporting = incomplete/inadequate reporting of methods, analyses, results or important information (e.g., selective reporting or overemphasis on significant secondary outcomes while ignoring non-significant primary outcomes). Misleading interpretation = interpretation of study results that could mislead readers (e.g., claiming equivalence for non-significant results). Inappropriate extrapolation = inappropriate generalisation of study results (e.g., recommending use in clinical practice based on an observational study). The protocol will identify labels, definitions and classification schemes from included reviews and may develop a new classification if schemes vary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility of reviews for inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Include publications that reported systematic or literature reviews on spin (aiming to examine spin in primary studies), assessing spin of primary studies of any design, reporting possible spin patterns and prevalence, and published in English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A review is systematic if authors make clear intent to perform a systematic review; publications that meet the methods-based definition (even if not using the word 'review') will be included. Full texts will be obtained when title/abstract insufficient. Included reviews may cover RCTs, non-RCTs, diagnostic/prognostic studies, economic studies, systematic reviews, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search strategy comprehensiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Search PubMed, EMBASE and SCOPUS using detailed search strings; limit to publications from 2010 onwards; use snowballing (backward citation searching) and PubMed 'similar articles' (top 20) to improve comprehensiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full search strategies are provided (Boolean strings and field tags). Searches were modified by a senior librarian. The snowballing strategy inspects references of eligible studies and checks similar articles for each eligible publication. Limiting to the last 10 years is acknowledged as a potential limitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data extraction — characteristics of included reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Extract review-level characteristics: publication year and first author; country/continent of first author; number of review authors; type of review (systematic vs literature); medical specialty; type of primary study evaluated in the review; sponsorship of the review; conflicts of interest of review authors; sampling methods used in the reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a standardised Excel form. Two reviewers will pilot extraction on a 10% sample to achieve ≥80% agreement; remainder extracted by one reviewer with a third reviewer checking a 10% random sample for accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data extraction — spin-related outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Extract spin-related outcomes from each review: sections where spin was assessed (abstracts, methods, results, conclusions); spin patterns identified including labels, definitions and classification schemes; prevalence of spin overall and by pattern based on original classification schemes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capture original classification schemes and labels verbatim when possible. If classification schemes differ across reviews, note these differences; plan for either quantitative pooling or qualitative description depending on comparability.

rubrics_metrics.name: AMSTAR-2 item — comprehensive literature search (Item 4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Did the review authors use a comprehensive literature search strategy?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Response options: Yes / Partial yes / No. 'Yes' indicates good methodological quality in this aspect. This item is considered critical for methodological quality assessment in this study; selective AMSTAR-2 items are applied as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: AMSTAR-2 item — list and justification of excluded studies (Item 7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Did the review authors provide a list of excluded studies and justify the exclusions?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Response options: Yes / Partial yes / No. Treated as a critical item for assessing methodological quality. Providing excluded studies and justifications improves transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: AMSTAR-2 item — account for risk of bias when interpreting results (Item 13)
rubrics_metrics.description: Did the review authors account for RoB in individual studies when interpreting/discussing the results of the review?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Response options: Yes / No. Considered a critical item. Accounting for RoB affects credibility of conclusions drawn by the review.

rubrics_metrics.name: AMSTAR-2 item — study selection in duplicate (Item 5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Did the review authors perform study selection in duplicate?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Response options: Yes / No. This non-critical item reduces selection errors and bias when 'Yes'.

rubrics_metrics.name: AMSTAR-2 item — data extraction in duplicate (Item 6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Did the review authors perform data extraction in duplicate?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Response options: Yes / No. Duplicate extraction reduces data extraction errors and improves reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: AMSTAR-2 item — describe included studies in adequate detail (Item 8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Did the review authors describe the included studies in adequate detail?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Response options: Yes / Partial yes / No. Adequate description aids interpretation and potential pooling.

rubrics_metrics.name: AMSTAR-2 item — report sources of funding for included studies (Item 10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Did the review authors report on the sources of funding for the studies included in the review?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Response options: Yes / No. Reporting funding sources helps identify potential sponsorship bias in primary studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: AMSTAR-2 item — report potential sources of conflict of interest for the review (Item 16)
rubrics_metrics.description: Did the review authors report any potential sources of conflict of interest, including any funding they received for conducting the review?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Response options: Yes / No. Transparency about conflicts of interest is required for assessing trustworthiness of reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of selective AMSTAR-2 items and separate consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply eight selected items from AMSTAR-2 that fit the purpose of this research, and do not combine items to create an overall score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate each item separately and consider the potential impact of each item on study results independently rather than computing a composite score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer training, piloting and agreement thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: Two reviewers will pilot selection, extraction and quality assessment procedures on sample subsets to achieve good agreement (at least 80%); typical pilots: 10% sample for selection/extraction to reach ≥80% agreement; piloting forms using 5% of included reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After piloting, refine forms as needed. A third reviewer will independently check a random 10% sample for accuracy. Disagreements resolved among all authors by consensus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical pooling decision rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Pool prevalences across reviews by meta-analysis only if classification schemes for spin (and thus definitions of overall spin) are comparable across included studies; otherwise describe prevalences qualitatively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If pooling: perform meta-analysis for single proportions using random effects models; assess heterogeneity with I^2 (heterogeneity considered large if I^2 > 50%). If large heterogeneity and >10 studies in meta-analysis, use multivariate meta-regression to explore sources. Use funnel plots to assess publication bias when >10 studies are included. Analyses conducted in R v3.3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling heterogeneity and publication bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Define thresholds and actions for heterogeneity and publication bias: I^2 > 50% considered large; multivariate meta-regression if heterogeneity large and number of included studies >10; funnel plot for publication bias when >10 studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These rules guide decisions on whether pooled estimates are meaningful and whether further analyses are indicated to explore variability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delphi consensus procedure for seriousness rating
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess seriousness of impact of each spin pattern via a Delphi consensus study with experts (authors of included reviews). Invite 10–15 experts (random sample if more than 15). Use iterative rounds with anonymity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experts rate seriousness on a 7-point scale (1 = not serious at all to 7 = extremely serious) and provide written justification. Present group anonymous ratings and justifications to participants between rounds and allow adjustments until stability (no further changes). Report individual ratings, mean scores, ranges and justifications; disagreement is an acceptable outcome. May develop a new classification of spin patterns with experts if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection criteria for Delphi experts
rubrics_metrics.description: Define experts as authors of included reviews; invite one author per included review (or two if too few reviews) aiming for 10–15 experts; if number of reviews >15, draw a random sample.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin with an initial video conference to clarify aims. The Delphi leverages anonymity to reduce group dynamics and gives equal weighting to expert opinions; limitations include potential lack of objectivity and reliance on expert opinion rather than experimental evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rating scale and reporting in Delphi
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a 7-point rating scale for seriousness; collect written justifications; calculate mean scores and present ranges for each spin pattern.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide participants with anonymous summary of ratings and justifications between rounds; if ratings are heterogeneous, provide explanations for disagreement. Final output includes individual ratings, means and justifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of reviews without explicit 'review' label
rubrics_metrics.description: Include publications that meet the methods-based definition of a review even if they do not use the word 'review' in titles/abstracts/main texts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine eligibility based on adopted methods. This broadens capture of relevant syntheses that functionally are reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time restriction on search (2010–present)
rubrics_metrics.description: Limit searches to the last 10 years (from 2010) because 2010 is the first identified publication to identify spin in clinical trials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors note this time restriction as a potential limitation since some meta-studies prior to 2010 might be relevant.
